title: RBI Implementation and Risk-Based Inspection Consulting
description: Setting up an RBI programme: governing procedure, team roles, method and software selection criteria, a pilot unit, rollout and keeping it current.
h1: Implementing a risk-based inspection programme that lasts
intro: For owners moving from calendar-based inspection to risk-based planning, and for those whose RBI programme produced one good study and then slowly went stale. Implementation is more than the first assessment: it means a governing procedure, approved risk criteria, defined roles, a method and a toolset that fit the site, a pilot that proves the approach, a rollout plan and a way of keeping everything current. This page sets out each of those pieces and what Atlantis provides, remotely, as risk-based inspection consulting.

highlights.p: The programme's rules come first: which equipment is in scope, which method applies, what data is required, who approves what, and how risk categories turn into inspection actions. Studies done without those rules produce results nobody can maintain consistently.

A pilot unit runs the full cycle, from data gathering to an approved plan, and tests the procedure, the data standard and the tools before the approach is repeated across the site. A problem found on one unit is a correction; the same problem found on twelve is a rework.

highlights.h: Built to be run by your team
highlights.p: Everything is set up so that your own people can carry the programme forward: documented decisions, a site loop library, clear triggers and coached analysts. An outside study that only its author can update has created a dependency rather than a programme.

sections.h: A study is not a programme
p: An RBI study produces a risk register and an inspection plan at one point in time. A programme is the procedures, people, data flows and review cycle that keep that register true as the plant changes. API RP 580, whose fourth edition (August 2023) is titled Elements of a Risk-Based Inspection Program, treats the subject that way: it covers programme planning, roles, responsibilities, training and qualifications, data collection, damage mechanism review, probability and consequence, risk management, documentation and the evergreening and reassessment that keep the assessment alive.

The commonest failure we see is not a bad first study. It is a competent first study that was never updated: inspection results stopped flowing back, changes of service were not reassessed, and a few years later the intervals rested on conditions that no longer existed. Implementation is mostly about preventing that.
A small set of controlled documents does most of the work. Atlantis drafts them with your team so that they reflect how your site actually operates:
list: RBI procedure: scope and equipment classes, the method for each, data requirements, the approval route for results and how RBI intervals relate to API 510, API 570, API 653 and any jurisdictional rules.
Risk criteria: the risk matrix or numerical risk targets approved by management, and the action each risk category requires.
Corrosion loop and damage mechanism library for the site, so that every unit is assessed against the same reference.
Data standard: the data required for each equipment type, accepted sources, default values and how defaults are flagged so they are never mistaken for measurements.
Inspection effectiveness tables: how the methods and coverage your inspectors actually use map to effectiveness categories for each damage mechanism.
Reassessment procedure: triggers from management of change, integrity operating window exceedances and inspection findings, and who initiates the update.
Roles and competence matrix, and the records and audit trail each assessment must leave behind.

p: A qualitative method uses structured judgement and a matrix; it is quick to apply and works well for screening or for smaller sites, but it depends heavily on who is in the room. Semi-quantitative schemes score factors numerically and give more consistency for moderate effort. The quantitative method in API RP 581 calculates probability and consequence from defined models; it gives the most defensible basis for long intervals and fine-grained planning, in exchange for a heavier data burden and the need for someone who understands the models.

Methods can be mixed. Many programmes screen everything qualitatively and spend quantitative effort on the items whose risk, consequence or interval justify it. ASME PCC-3 (2022 edition) offers a further framework, and many operators have their own RBI standard that takes precedence over both. The procedure should say which method applies to which equipment and why, so that the choice is not reopened for every study.

sections.h: Selecting RBI software on criteria, not demonstrations
p: Most programmes beyond a few hundred items run in a commercial RBI package, and the choice outlives the people who make it. Atlantis does not resell any RBI package and works with whichever one you choose, or with structured spreadsheets for smaller scopes. Useful selection criteria include:
list: Methodology fidelity: which edition of API RP 581 it implements, and whether every intermediate value can be inspected rather than only the final risk.
Ability to hold your own RBI standard or risk criteria where they differ from the published method.
A data model that fits your equipment: circuits and monitoring locations, tank shell courses and bottoms, exchanger bundles and relief devices.
Integration with your maintenance system and inspection data system, so that results and work orders do not live in separate worlds.
Open import and export, so the data remains yours if you change tools.
Versioning and audit trail: who changed what, when and why, and the ability to reproduce an old assessment exactly.
Clear handling of default values and data quality flags.
How code edition changes are delivered and validated, and who on your side will maintain the configuration.

p: The pilot is chosen for learning value: a unit with reasonable records and engaged people, or the one whose turnaround is next, so the plan is used for real straight away. It runs the full cycle, including the inspection the plan calls for and the update that follows, because the steps most likely to fail are the ones after the report is issued.

At the end of the pilot the procedure, the data standard, the loop library and the effectiveness tables are revised with what was learned, and the effort required per unit is known from experience rather than estimated. Only then is the approach repeated elsewhere.

Rollout is normally sequenced by the turnaround schedule, so each unit's plan is ready before the work it is meant to shape. Data gathering for later units can run in parallel with workshops for earlier ones. Consistency checks across units catch drift in how mechanisms are assigned or how effectiveness is credited. Until a unit's assessment is approved by your inspector, its existing time-based intervals stay in force, which keeps the transition safe and auditable.

Each study is delivered remotely through a data room and video workshops, with field verification done by your own inspectors. For US facilities, Atlantis can also supply UT, MT, PT and VT technicians to close data gaps found during rollout and to carry out conventional NDT the plans call for.

p: A programme stays healthy when changes flow into it automatically: management of change requests ask whether the RBI is affected, integrity operating window exceedances are reviewed for their effect on damage rates, and every inspection report is checked against the rate the assessment assumed. On top of those triggers sits a fixed review cycle, set within the limits of the inspection codes you work to.

Simple indicators show whether the programme is alive: the share of items with a current assessment, overdue inspections, open data gaps and unreviewed exceedances. Periodic internal audits check that decisions are documented and that intervals still have a basis. Where damage needs fitness-for-service evaluation, the programme routes it to your engineer, because Atlantis does not perform that work.

faqs.q: What does RBI implementation actually involve?
faqs.a: Setting up the procedure, risk criteria, data standard and roles that govern the programme; choosing a method and, where needed, a software package; proving the approach on a pilot unit; rolling it out across the site; and putting in place the triggers and review cycle that keep it current. The first risk study is one step in that sequence, not the whole job.

faqs.q: Should we start with one unit or the whole site?
faqs.a: One unit. A pilot tests the procedure, the data standard and the tools on real equipment, including the inspection and update that follow the plan. What is learned there is built into the documents before the approach is repeated, which saves far more effort across the site than the pilot itself takes.

faqs.q: Do we need dedicated RBI software?
faqs.a: Not for every scope. Small programmes can run well in controlled spreadsheets. Once the register reaches several hundred items, or you want quantitative API RP 581 calculations, a dedicated package becomes worthwhile for consistency and audit trail. Choose it on methodology transparency, data model fit, integration, open export and versioning rather than on the demonstration.

faqs.q: Do our time-based intervals stay in force during rollout?
faqs.a: They should. Until a unit's assessment has been completed, reviewed and approved by your inspector, its existing code-based intervals remain the basis for inspection. That keeps the transition auditable and avoids a period in which no approved interval exists for some equipment.

faqs.q: Who should be on the RBI team?
faqs.a: An RBI lead or analyst, the inspection lead, a corrosion or materials specialist, the unit process engineer and an experienced operator, with maintenance planning and a systems person involved as results turn into work. Management sponsorship matters too, because someone has to approve the risk criteria and settle priority disputes.

faqs.q: What is a risk target, and who sets it?
faqs.a: A risk target is the level of risk at which an item needs inspection or other action, expressed as a matrix position or a numerical value. The owner's management sets and approves it; neither API RP 580 nor API RP 581 sets it for you. The target belongs in the risk criteria document so every study is judged against the same line.

faqs.q: How do we stop the programme going stale?
faqs.a: Connect it to the processes that change the plant: management of change, integrity operating window monitoring and inspection reporting. Add a fixed review cycle and a few indicators, such as items with a current assessment, overdue inspections and open data gaps, and review them regularly. Programmes decay when results stop flowing back in.

faqs.q: What does risk-based inspection consulting from Atlantis cover?
faqs.a: Remote gap assessment, procedure and criteria drafting, loop libraries, pilot and rollout studies, coaching of your analysts and periodic reassessment, plus conventional NDT for US facilities. Intervals are approved by your inspector of record, and every document is written so that your own people can maintain it.
